channel.title: Global Arbitration Review - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Global Arbitration Review (globalarbitrationreview.com)

item.title: Bangladeshi state entity wins limited damages over gas field blowout
item.description: An ICSID tribunal has ordered a subsidiary of Canada’s Niko Resources to pay a small fraction of the US$800 million in compensation sought by Bangladesh’s national oil company over a blowout at a gas field two decades ago.

item.title: Wordstone hires former US investment arbitration chief
item.description: David Bigge has left his role as chief of investment arbitration at the US Department of State to help GAR 30 firm Wordstone Dispute Resolution launch a new office in Washington, DC.

item.title: Saudi power plant claims play out in Bahrain
item.description: A Saudi state-owned utility is facing three Bahrain-seated UNCITRAL arbitrations brought by contractors on a billion-dollar power plant project, with awards in two of the cases expected soon.

item.title: India defeats Korean utility’s treaty claim
item.description: An UNCITRAL tribunal has dismissed a US$400 million treaty claim brought against India by a subsidiary of a South Korean state-owned electric utility over an investment in a gas-based power plant.

item.title: RPC hires new India practice head
item.description: Ankit Goyal has left Allen & Gledhill to lead the India practice at RPC in Singapore.

item.title: Could Saudi Arabia face treaty claims over downscaling of giga-projects?
item.description: A panel at Riyadh International Disputes Week discussed whether Saudi Arabia could face investment treaty claims over its decision to scale back its flagship giga-project Neom and several other multitrillion-dollar developments.

item.title: Skadden hires another partner from Latham
item.description: Samuel Pape has left Latham & Watkins for Skadden Arps Slate Meagher & Flom in London, weeks after Sophie Lamb KC made the same move.

item.title: UK court to assess India’s challenge to Gibson Dunn in Devas dispute
item.description: A London court has ruled in India’s favour on preliminary issues in a dispute over whether Gibson Dunn has the authority to represent three Mauritian entities in an investment treaty claim.

item.title: Canada faces ICSID claim over Russia sanctions
item.description: A billionaire who renounced his Russian citizenship has made good on his threat to bring an ICSID claim worth at least US$250 million against Canada over its refusal to take him off its sanctions list.

item.title: Abu Dhabi fund wins claim over collapse of Austrian property empire
item.description: Abu Dhabi sovereign wealth fund Mubadala has reportedly won a €700 million ICC award against affiliates of Austria’s troubled Signa property group.
